title: Sensing Principles: How Physical Effects Become Electrical Signals

contract.reader: An engineering student or engineer new to sensors, with basic circuit theory, who wants to understand what is inside the sensors they select
contract.problem: Thousands of sensor products seem unrelated; the reader needs the few physical effects behind them and what each implies for use
contract.outcome: Classify a sensor by energy domain and family, state each family's governing equation, estimate a typical signal size, and say what each principle cannot do (static force for piezoelectric, absolute temperature for thermocouples, temperature-independent pH slope)
contract.contribution: Each principle with one governing equation, one worked number from typical constants and one practical consequence, framed by a families table and closed by a selection table by measurand
contract.evidence: Textbook physics and typical material constants; Fraden (2016); Pallas-Areny and Webster (2001); Regtien and Dertien (2018); Webster and Eren, Eds. (2014)
contract.limitations: Survey depth; typical constants, not product data; conditioning circuits left to the next entry

findings.problem: The page has no figure; the thermocouple circuit (measuring junction, reference junction at the instrument terminals) and the LVDT coil arrangement are described only in prose
findings.whyItMatters: Why a thermocouple measures a difference is one of the three questions the opening promises to answer; a schematic answers it at a glance (standards 6.8)
findings.action: Add a generated, captioned thermocouple circuit schematic to Section 6 (optionally an LVDT schematic to Section 4.1)
findings.acceptance: The live page shows a captioned thermocouple schematic in Section 6, legible at 360 px in light and dark mode
